subject: research/chip-mac-lanes
professional: a senior computer architect / ML-accelerator designer who sizes MAC arrays; first checks: do the cycle counts follow from the schedule, is the RTL bit-exact including saturation, is the figure of merit (cells x cycles) robust to clock period and to equivalent RTL rewrites, and is 'powers of two win' a real effect or a tiling/divisibility artefact

evidence.correctness: Installed Yosys 0.33 and Icarus 12.0 (the README's versions) and reran 10 of the 40 headline rows (F=16: P=1,4,6,8,16; F=32: P=8,12,13,16,20) with a scratch script calling flow.simulate/flow.score exactly as experiments/run.py does: every row reproduced results.txt to the cell (e.g. '16 8 53 [53] 3560 38 188680 True', '32 13 85 [85] 14697 63 1249245 True'), measured cycles equal the formula, RTL == NumPy on all 32 vectors. Independently recomputed all 40 cycle counts from the README formula 2 + ceil(16/P)(F+1) + ceil(4/P)17 (hand check: P=3,F=16 -> 2+6*17+2*17 = 138) and all 40 cells x cycles products: 0 mismatches. Recomputed every ranking claim from results.txt: top-3 at F=16 (8:188680, 4:198099, 16:217548), F=32 (16:360932, 8:372045, 4:512494), best non-power P=6 44.2% behind and P=20 62.1% behind, P=1 worst power of two, P=17..20 all 52 cycles with P=20 smallest at 11251 cells: all match. The 'earlier numbers reproduce exactly' claim checked against research/chip-systolic-hidewide/experiments/results.txt lines 9-19: P=4, 8, 16 at both F match. Not 4: the output saturation path (QMIN/QMAX clamp, layer 1) is never exercised by any vector in the tests or the headline run (raw outputs range -5..+3 against [-8, 7]), so 'bit for bit' is proven only on the non-saturating path.
evidence.completeness: README promises: tests (ran, 4 pass in 14.1 s against 'about 30 s'), the P=1..20 x F=16,32 sweep with RTL check and formula check (40 rows present, 10 rerun identically), results table and bullets (all backed by results.txt), figure (experiments/lanes.png committed; figure.py not rerun here because matplotlib is absent in the container, it reads only results.txt). Live page link https://marisstella.app/research/chip-mac-lanes/ could not be loaded (proxy, curl 000) and served-copy.mjs reports no product index.html for this path, so the page was not verified. No stubs or TODOs in the code.
evidence.verification: PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests: 4 tests OK in 14.1 s. The RTL-vs-NumPy-and-formula test is a real oracle (seeded change (fan+1)->(fan+2) in cycles() was caught, 2 failures). But two of three seeded mutants survived: weakening the layer-1 QMIN clamp in the generated RTL (no test vector saturates) and dropping MUX from the ABC gate library (changes every cell count, i.e. every headline number, while test_area_grows_with_lanes only checks that P=2,4,8 are sorted). Nothing pins any committed cell count or the cells x cycles metric to results.txt.
evidence.craft: Read baseline_gen.py, flow.py, model.py, run.py, figure.py, test_mac_lanes.py. Small and readable, run.py writes results incrementally, figure is regenerated from results only. Defects: baseline_gen.py docstrings still describe chip-accel's F=8 design ('fan-in 8', '8 MAC cycles', line 3 and 15) and the generated header says 'chip_accel.gen' (line 49); model.py:45 comment refers to F=8; flow.py:45,46,68 open() without close (ResourceWarning on every test run); pyproject.toml declares no dependencies (numpy is required); the engine is a third copy of chip-accel's generator (via chip-systolic-hidewide), so fixes do not propagate. Padded lanes (n >= H) still compute with truncated, aliased ROM indices (n is cw bits, wrom takes nw bits); harmless to outputs because write-back masks them, but it is hardware synthesis cannot remove.
evidence.claims: Each numeric claim in README Results and the four bullets is backed by results.txt (checked above). The method, limitations (gate counts only, depth not timing, one seed, generator artefact possible) and 'produced with AI assistance' are stated plainly. The cause of the cell-count non-monotonicity is correctly labelled untested. Gap: 'Non-powers of two never win' is presented as a finding, but with H=16 and 4 outputs the divisors of 16 are exactly the powers of two, so 'power of two' and 'divides H without padding' are perfectly confounded; the README does not say so and its next step (H=8, H=32) keeps the confound. Live page claim not verifiable here.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun and extend it: the harness reproduces exactly and runs P=1..20 in about 15 min. Nearest prior work: HLS/accelerator design-space exploration of parallelism (unroll / PE count) factors, e.g. Zhang et al., FPGA 2015 (roofline-guided unroll-factor DSE for CNN accelerators) and the standard HLS guidance that unroll factors should divide the trip count; Timeloop/SCALE-Sim style mapping analysis gives the same idle-lane accounting. None is cited (README 'Builds on' names only sibling projects). The result is mostly what that literature predicts (P > H cannot cut cycles; non-divisors waste lanes), plus a generator-specific area effect. Novelty is not loudly overstated, but it is an increment on chip-systolic-hidewide (which already found P=8/P=16), not a new finding.
evidence.domain: Cells x cycles is an area-delay proxy that ignores clock period, and the depth column varies 38..79 gates across P. Recomputed with depth as a crude period proxy (cells x cycles x depth): F=16 still 8 < 4 < 16, F=32 still 16 < 8 < 4, so the winners are robust. Also tested a functionally equivalent RTL rewrite in a scratch copy (gate each lane's MAC with n < N so padded lanes add 0): RTL still bit-exact, cell counts drop 15-25% (F=16 P=16 6043->4639, F=32 P=16 6941->5203) and the winners do not change (F=16 P=8 152905 < P=16 167004 < P=4 168606; F=32 P=16 270556 < P=8 301410), and the P=13 vs P=16 non-monotonicity persists (13385 vs 5203). So the ranking is robust but absolute cell counts are generator-specific by about a quarter. A senior architect would still want: memory/weight traffic (weights are combinational ROM), timing from STA, power, and an H that is not a power of two before concluding anything about powers of two.

defects.what: Every headline number is unpinned by tests: dropping MUX from the ABC gate library (changes all cell counts) and weakening the layer-1 QMIN clamp both leave all 4 tests green. No test compares any cell count with results.txt, and no vector in the tests or the 32-vector headline check saturates an output (raw range -5..+3 vs [-8, 7]), so 'bit for bit' never covers the clamp logic

'Non-powers of two never win' is perfectly confounded with divisibility: with H=16 and 4 outputs the divisors of 16 are exactly {1,2,4,8,16}, so padding loss and the generator's grp*P multiplier both line up with 'power of two'. The README does not say so, and the proposed H=8/H=32 follow-up keeps the confound; an H of 12 or 24 is needed to separate them

No prior work outside the repo is cited. The lane-count result is what accelerator/HLS design-space exploration predicts (unroll/PE factors that divide the trip count; P > H cannot cut cycles; e.g. Zhang et al. FPGA 2015, Timeloop, SCALE-Sim), and cells x cycles ignores clock period, memory and power
Docstrings and generated header describe chip-accel's F=8 design: 'layer L has fan-in 8', '8 MAC cycles', 'Generated by chip_accel.gen', model.py comment '= 2*wb+5 at F = 8'
pyproject.toml declares no dependencies although numpy is imported (README's venv step installs it by hand); flow.py writes temp files with unclosed open() (ResourceWarning on each run)

Padded lanes (grp*P+j >= N) still multiply by ROM weights indexed with a truncated n (cw-bit n passed to an nw-bit port), so synthesis keeps their MACs; outputs are unaffected (write-back masks them), but gating them to 0 cuts cells 15-25% while keeping the ranking, so absolute cell counts are generator-specific by about a quarter

verdict: The numbers are right and reproduce: with Yosys 0.33 and Icarus 12.0 installed fresh, 10 of the 40 sweep rows rerun identical to results.txt, all 40 cycle counts and cells x cycles products recompute from the schedule formula, every ranking and percentage in the README checks out, and the P=4/8/16 cross-check against chip-systolic-hidewide holds. The winners (P=8 at F=16, P=16 at F=32) survive weighting by gate depth and a functionally equivalent RTL rewrite. It does not meet the bar because verification misses where the result lives (2 of 3 seeded mutants survive: the gate library behind every cell count, and the output clamp no vector reaches), and as research it is a careful increment: 'non-powers of two never win' is confounded with 'divides H=16', no outside prior work is cited, and the merit ignores clock period, memory and power. Finished (everything claimed runs), median 3, verification 2.
